> 道常無為而無不為。侯王若能守之，萬物將自化.

Chapter 36 gave an eye: see the rising and falling as one movement, and take the hand back.

Chapter 37 asks the next question — where does the hand go once it comes back?

The answer is not simply "onto yourself," because there is something in yourself that also wants to act: the thing that wants to arrange, to correct, to make it become what I want.

This chapter supplies one medicine, and it is two characters: 樸.

## 無為而無不為

> 道常無為而無不為.

Not "does nothing and yet everything gets done" as a slogan. 為 in its old form is a hand pulling an elephant — the character is literally effort applied to a large thing.

無為 is not inaction; it is action that is not 為 in that sense: no hand pulling against the grain of the thing.

無不為 is not omnipotence. It is: nothing is left undone, because nothing was blocked. The two halves are the same statement from opposite sides.

## 自化

> 萬物將自化.

化 contains 化's own old association with 教 — transformation, but the kind that happens by being brought along rather than being commanded.

自化: they transform of themselves. The ruler's contribution is the condition, not the change.

## 化而欲作

> 化而欲作，吾將鎮之以無名之樸.

They transform, and then 欲作 — the desire rises. 作 is the character for 起: to get up, to start up. Something begins to stir.

Not desire as sin — desire as ignition. The transformation is going well, and precisely then the impulse appears: now that it is moving, let me steer it.

鎮 is to press down, to steady, to anchor. Not to argue with it, not to persuade it, not to explain why it should stop.

The medicine is a piece of unworked wood pressed on the spot. It is not an argument; it is a weight.

## 無名之樸

樸 is the log before the carpenter — the same 樸 as in chapters 28 and 32.

無名 is the crucial qualifier: a log with no name has no rank, no scale, no claim. You cannot argue with it, because there is nothing to argue against. You can only be pressed by it.

This is why the sedative works: what it presses down is not the person, it is the spark. The impulse to arrange does not survive contact with something that has no arrangement to offer.

## 不欲以靜，天下將自定

Not desiring, therefore still; the world settles of itself.

自定 — settles itself. The last word of the 道 section, and it is the same 自 as 自然: no external hand.

## The shape of the book's first half

The received text ends the Dao section here. It opened with 道可道，非恒道；名可名，非恒名 and closes with 無為 and 無名之樸.

One end is 無為, the other is 無名 — the same sentence seen from its two ends: what cannot be named cannot be managed.

## A test

Notice the moment in any process you are running when it starts to work. That is 欲作. The instinct is to intervene at exactly the point where intervention is most expensive.
